title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus
plain: There is a problem on the high speed CAN network, the wiring network the car's computers use to talk to each other.
symptoms: Several warning lights on at once
Some gauges or features may stop working
Car may not start in some cases

causes.name: Damaged, chafed or corroded network wiring
Loose or corroded connector at a module
A failed module dragging the network down
Water getting into a connector
Low battery voltage

checks: Test the battery and charging voltage
Check network resistance at the diagnostic port (about 60 ohms on most high speed CAN networks)
Unplug modules one at a time to find one shorting the network
Inspect wiring in areas that see water, heat or movement
fix: Find and repair the damaged network wire or connector, or replace the module that is shorting the network.
examples: Often appears with many other U codes after water damage or a wiring repair
drive: Use care. Lost communication between modules can affect gauges, brakes, steering assist or the transmission. If several warnings come on, the brakes or steering feel different, or it stalls, don't keep driving; have it towed. Otherwise go straight to a shop soon.
test_first: Check battery voltage and grounds, test the network wiring for shorts or opens, and unplug modules one at a time to find the one pulling the network down before replacing any module.

causes.name: Network wiring short or open

Low battery voltage

title: Lost Communication With ECM/PCM "A"
plain: Other computers in the car have stopped hearing from the engine computer (ECM/PCM). It runs the engine, so other modules rely on it for engine speed, temperature and other data.
symptoms: Check engine light and several other warning lights on
Car may not start, or may stall
Gauges such as the tachometer may stop working
Transmission may stay in one gear

causes.name: Engine computer lost power or ground (blown fuse, bad relay or corroded ground)
Damaged, corroded or loose network wiring or connector
Weak battery or low system voltage
Failed engine computer (ECM/PCM)
Another module shorting out the network

checks: Test the battery and charging voltage first
Check the fuses, power and ground for the engine computer (ECM/PCM)
See which modules answer a scan tool to narrow down the break
Inspect network wiring and connectors near the module
fix: Restore power, ground or wiring to the engine computer (ECM/PCM); replace the module only after those test good.

cost.job: Repair engine computer power, ground or network wiring

examples: Often set during a dead battery or jump start; clear and recheck after the battery is fixed
drive: Use care. If the engine stalls, won't start, or several warnings and gauges drop out, don't rely on the car; have it towed, since a stall in traffic is dangerous. If it runs normally with just a light on, get it to a shop soon.
test_first: Check the engine computer's power, grounds and fuses, battery voltage, and network wiring at its connector before replacing the engine computer.

title: Lost Communication With TCM
plain: Other computers in the car have stopped hearing from the transmission control module (TCM). It controls the automatic transmission.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Transmission may stay in one gear (limp mode)
Harsh shifts or no shifts
Gear indicator may be blank

causes.name: The transmission control module (TCM) lost power or ground (blown fuse or bad ground)
Damaged, corroded or loose network wiring or connector
Weak battery or low system voltage
Failed transmission control module (TCM)
Another module shorting out the network

checks: Test the battery and charging voltage first
Check the fuses, power and ground for the transmission control module (TCM)
See which modules answer a scan tool to narrow down the break
Inspect network wiring and connectors near the module
fix: Restore power, ground or wiring to the transmission control module (TCM); replace the module only after those test good.

cost.job: Repair transmission module power, ground or wiring

drive: Often drivable with care, but the transmission may stay in one gear, giving slow acceleration or high RPM. Avoid highways if it won't shift. If it slips or more warnings pile up, get it checked right away.
test_first: Check the transmission computer's power, ground and fuses, and its network wiring and connectors, before replacing the transmission computer.
